liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Hard To Handle** (1 review): Phil's funky, hammering bass lines in this song hooked the reviewer on the Dead [7]
- **Sugar Magnolia** (1 review): Garcia uses his wah-wah pedal on this song [12]
- **Lovelight** (1 review): Reviewer says the Lovelight crowns the show [8]

## Setlist highlights

- **Pigpen Rap (Female companionship rap**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]
- **Business rap**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]

## The recordings

- **gd1971-02-20.sbd.cantor-crouch-diebert-gmb.85912.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 28 songs; 155 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [1]. Said about its sound: Both the Betty Cantor and newer sources sound brilliant and lively, with a few annoying dropouts; A whine with peaks near 8100 and 15700 Hz was reduced with notch filtering [1][14]
- **gd1971-02-20.sbd.cantor.orf.6188.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 156 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [2]. Said about its sound: Classic 1971 sound; reviewer suggests applying EQ during playback [12]
- **gd71-02-20.sbd.orf.111.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 151 min; rated 4.33/5 by 12 [3]. Said about its sound: Recording is clear and crisp, with Phil high in the mix; reminiscent of the Skull and Roses album; Betty Cantor-sourced sound is brilliant and lively, though a few dropouts occur; both guitars sound jangly [10][13]
- **gd1971-02-20.sbd.miller.116617.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 160 min; rated 4.33/5 by 6 [4]

## Around the show

- Early on there is chuckling, then Bobby sings a line about Moses riding in to buy a car [11]
- The vibe is quite laid back, but the playing is strong with dynamite jamming [13]
- Reviewer finds the vibe laid back and speculates the band might be hungover [14]
- Reviewer says the Port Chester run introduced several new Dead staples and marked a major turning point in direction [7]
- Reviewer names this their favorite show of the Port Chester run [8]
- Reviewer prefers 1971's single-drummer sound, with room for Phil, over the funkier 1979 lineup [10]
- Reviewer says Feb 18 gets the accolades from the run, but this show deserves recognition too [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1971-02-20.sbd.cantor-crouch-diebert-gmb.85912.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Original WBOTB DATs procured & circulated in 1996 by Jace Crouch and Tim Deibert. Thanks to trailmix for providing the lineaged master DAT  for transfer.; transferred by Transfer and mastering by Chris L.; source: 7" two track BBD reel w/ Dolby A @ 7 1/2 ips > PCM501ES (beta) > PCM501ES analog out > Dolby A decoder > Apogee filter > analog in PCMF1/PCM501ES analog out >… [1]. Also: Reel flips and short gaps in Casey Jones, Bird Song and Lovelight were crossfaded using samples of matching beats [1]
- **gd1971-02-20.sbd.cantor.orf.6188.shnf**: source: 7" 2-track Betty Reel w/ dolby A @ 7 1/2 ips > PCM501ES @ 44.056 KHz PCM501ES analog out > dolby A decoder > analog in Fostex D5 @ 48KHz > DATx32 [2]
- **gd71-02-20.sbd.orf.111.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Leigh Orf; source: Soundboard [3]. Also: Show fits in order onto two 80-minute discs, in the reviewer's view; Source is the Betty Cantor tape; uploader removed interference whine, as done for other Port Chester shows, using two different programs [3][6]
- **gd1971-02-20.sbd.miller.116617.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> CD [4]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Paul Kreizenbeck Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead at The Capitol Theatre (2/20/1971) by Paul Kreizenbeck | Relix](https://relix.shop/collections/grateful-dead-at-the-capitol-theatre-2-20-1971-by-paul-kreizenbeck) [20]
- Poster by crepuscularthad.blogspot.com: [Brokedown Palace: The Capitol Theatre and the Grateful Dead](https://crepuscularthad.blogspot.com/2017/03/capitol-theatre-and-grateful-dead.html) [21]
- Poster by Chuck Sperry Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead at The Capitol Theatre, 1970-1971 - Posters, T-Shirts, H | Relix](https://relix.shop/collections/grateful-dead-at-the-capitol-theatre-1970-1971?page=2) [22]
